components.note: 犭 (animal, 反犬旁) — marks beasts, as in 猫 cat, 狗 dog, 猪 pig.
师 (shī) gives the exact sound, as in 老师 teacher.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 动物园里的狮子正在晒太阳。
example.pinyin: dòngwùyuán lǐ de shīzi zhèngzài shài tàiyáng.
example.english: The lion at the zoo is sunbathing.
example.fact: A lion's roar can be heard from up to 8 kilometers away, produced by a specialized flat, square-shaped larynx and vocal cords that let air pass through with less resistance than in other big cats, generating the lowest, loudest roar of any cat species.

examples.hanzi: 狮子是草原上的王者。
examples.pinyin: Shīzi shì cǎoyuán shàng de wángzhě.
examples.english: The lion is the king of the grassland.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们很喜欢看狮子表演。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen hěn xǐhuan kàn shīzi biǎoyǎn.
examples.english: The children love watching the lions perform.

components.note: 旅 (travel) — a flag with people gathered under it: a troop on the march, then travellers on a journey.
辶 (movement) — marks roads and travel, as in 过, 进, 送; 途 is a road or route.
余 (yú) is a loose hint for tú; 涂 tú shares it.

example.hanzi: 这次长途旅途让他学到了很多东西。
example.pinyin: zhè cì chángtú lǚtú ràng tā xuédào le hěn duō dōngxi.
example.english: This long journey taught him a lot.
example.fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway, completed in 1916, stretches over 9,289 kilometers between Moscow and Vladivostok, making it the longest single railway line in the world — a full end-to-end journey takes about seven days and crosses eight time zones.

examples.hanzi: 祝你旅途愉快！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ lǚtú yúkuài!
examples.english: Have a pleasant trip!

examples.hanzi: 漫长的旅途中，他一直在看书。
examples.pinyin: Màncháng de lǚtú zhōng, tā yìzhí zài kàn shū.
examples.english: During the long journey, he kept reading.

meanings: climax (of a story, a competition etc)

components.note: 高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.
氵 (water) — the tide; also in 海 sea, 河 river.
朝 (cháo) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 嘲 cháo.

example.hanzi: 电影的高潮部分让观众紧张得不敢呼吸。
example.pinyin: diànyǐng de gāocháo bùfen ràng guānzhòng jǐnzhāng de bùgǎn hūxī.
example.english: The climax of the movie made the audience so tense they could barely breathe.
example.fact: Ocean tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon combined with the Sun's weaker pull; the Bay of Fundy in Canada experiences the largest tidal range on Earth, with water levels rising and falling by as much as 16 meters between high and low tide.

examples.hanzi: 比赛进入了高潮，观众都站了起来。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài jìnrù le gāocháo, guānzhòng dōu zhàn le qǐlái.
examples.english: The match reached its climax, and the audience all stood up.

examples.hanzi: 晚会在歌声中达到了高潮。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnhuì zài gēshēng zhōng dádào le gāocháo.
examples.english: The party reached its peak with the singing.

components.note: 冫 (ice, 两点水) — marks cold and freezing, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 决; 凉 is cool, as in 凉快 pleasantly cool.
京 (jīng) — loose sound hint (liáng vs jīng); same part in 凉 liáng and 谅 liàng.

example.hanzi: 天气凉了，多穿点儿衣服。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì liáng le, duō chuān diǎnr yīfu.
example.english: It has turned cool, so wear a bit more.
example.fact: 凉 is pleasantly or mildly cold, milder than 冷: 凉快 (nicely cool), 凉爽, 凉菜 (cold dishes). Tea or food that has gone cold is 凉了; the word also appears in slang 凉了 meaning "we're doomed."

examples.hanzi: 这杯水有点凉，我想喝热的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi shuǐ yǒudiǎn liáng, wǒ xiǎng hē rè de.
examples.english: This water is a bit cold. I want something hot.

examples.hanzi: 夏天晚上很凉快。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǎnshang hěn liángkuai.
examples.english: Summer nights are nice and cool.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 拽 is pulling or dragging, as in 拉拽.
曳 (yè) — same sound: 拽 yè (also zhuài). 曳 also sounds out 洩 xiè.

example.hanzi: 他拽着我的手不放。
example.pinyin: Tā zhuài zhe wǒ de shǒu bú fàng.
example.english: He held on to my hand and would not let go.
example.fact: 拽 means to tug or drag. In mainland slang, 他很拽 means someone acts cool and arrogant, as if swaggering. It has two other readings: zhuāi (dialect, to throw) and yè (literary, to pull).

examples.hanzi: 别拽我的衣服，我自己走。
examples.pinyin: Bié zhuài wǒ de yīfu, wǒ zìjǐ zǒu.
examples.english: Don't pull my clothes, I will walk myself.

examples.hanzi: 小孩拽着妈妈往前走。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái zhuài zhe māma wǎng qián zǒu.
examples.english: The child pulled his mother forward.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and gifts, as in 财, 货, 贵; 赞 is to help or praise, as with a gift.

example.hanzi: 大家都称赞他的汉语说得好。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu chēngzàn tā de Hànyǔ shuō de hǎo.
example.english: Everyone praised how well he speaks Chinese.
example.fact: 赞 is to praise: 称赞, 赞成 (to agree with), 赞助 (to sponsor). On Chinese social media, 点赞 means to give a "like," and 很赞 or 太赞了 is slang for "awesome."

examples.hanzi: 老师赞他的字写得好。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zàn tā de zì xiě de hǎo.
examples.english: The teacher praised him for his nice handwriting.

examples.hanzi: 大家都赞成这个办法。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zànchéng zhège bànfǎ.
examples.english: Everyone approves of this method.

components.note: 月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.
人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".

example.hanzi: 士兵必须无条件服从命令。
example.pinyin: shìbīng bìxū wútiáojiàn fúcóng mìnglìng.
example.english: Soldiers must obey orders unconditionally.
example.fact: The 1961 Milgram experiment at Yale University found that roughly 65% of ordinary participants were willing to administer what they believed were painful electric shocks to a stranger simply because an authority figure in a lab coat instructed them to continue, revealing how strongly situational authority can override personal conscience.

examples.hanzi: 孩子应该服从老师的安排。
examples.pinyin: Háizi yīnggāi fúcóng lǎoshī de ānpái.
examples.english: Children should follow the teacher's arrangements.

examples.hanzi: 少数要服从多数。
examples.pinyin: Shǎoshù yào fúcóng duōshù.
examples.english: The minority should defer to the majority.

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 请; 诚 is honest speech.
成 (chéng) — same sound — 诚 is chéng, like 成; 成 also sounds out 城 chéng.

example.hanzi: 他用真诚的态度向大家道歉。
example.pinyin: tā yòng zhēnchéng de tàidù xiàng dàjiā dàoqiàn.
example.english: He apologized to everyone with a sincere attitude.
example.fact: Psychologists have found that a genuine "Duchenne smile" — named after the 19th-century French neurologist Guillaume Duchenne who first studied it — involves involuntary contraction of the muscles around the eyes, not just the mouth, which is why fake smiles are often detectable even to casual observers.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个真诚的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge zhēnchéng de péngyou.
examples.english: He is a sincere friend.

examples.hanzi: 请接受我真诚的感谢。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiēshòu wǒ zhēnchéng de gǎnxiè.
examples.english: Please accept my sincere thanks.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person and his word: 言 (speech) beside it gives a person who keeps his word, hence "trust, believe".
言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters, as in 说, 请, 谢.
心 (heart) — 心 marks thoughts and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感; 念 is to think of someone.
今 (jīn) — loose hint — 念 is niàn; 今 also sounds out 琴 qín and 含 hán, and means "now".

example.hanzi: 坚定的信念帮助她度过了最困难的时期。
example.pinyin: jiāndìng de xìnniàn bāngzhù tā dùguò le zuì kùnnán de shíqī.
example.english: Her firm conviction helped her get through the most difficult period.
example.fact: Ernest Shackleton's crew survived nearly two years stranded in Antarctica after their ship Endurance was crushed by ice in 1915; historians often credit their survival to Shackleton's unshakeable belief that he would bring every one of his 27 men home alive, which he ultimately did.

examples.hanzi: 他有一个坚定的信念：努力一定有回报。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu yí ge jiāndìng de xìnniàn: nǔlì yídìng yǒu huíbào.
examples.english: He has a firm belief that hard work will pay off.

examples.hanzi: 没有信念，就很难坚持下去。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu xìnniàn, jiù hěn nán jiānchí xiàqù.
examples.english: Without conviction, it's hard to keep going.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).
口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫; 嘴 is a mouth or lips.
觜 (zuǐ) — same sound — 嘴 is zuǐ, like 觜.

example.hanzi: “住嘴!”妈妈生气地喊道。
example.pinyin: “zhùzuǐ!” māma shēngqì de hǎn dào.
example.english: "Shut up!" mom shouted angrily.
example.fact: The human vocal cords can vibrate anywhere from about 60 to 1,000 times per second depending on pitch, and sustained shouting at high volume can cause tiny tears in the vocal fold tissue, which is why singers and voice coaches train people to project sound using breath support rather than throat strain.

examples.hanzi: 你们都住嘴，听老师说。
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen dōu zhùzuǐ, tīng lǎoshī shuō.
examples.english: All of you be quiet and listen to the teacher.

examples.hanzi: 他被弟弟气得大喊：“住嘴！”
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi dìdi qì de dà hǎn: “Zhùzuǐ!”
examples.english: His younger brother made him so angry that he shouted, “Shut up!”

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.
八 (eight) — originally two strokes pulling apart, meaning divide; that sense is in 分 divide, 公 public and 半 half.

example.hanzi: 这是他第八次参加马拉松比赛。
example.pinyin: zhè shì tā dì bā cì cānjiā mǎlāsōng bǐsài.
example.english: This is the eighth time he has taken part in a marathon.
example.fact: The modern marathon distance of 42.195 kilometers wasn't standardized until the 1908 London Olympics, when organizers extended the course so the race could start at Windsor Castle and finish in front of the royal box at the stadium — the odd extra 195 meters has stuck ever since.

examples.hanzi: 我们住在大楼的第八层。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhù zài dàlóu de dì bā céng.
examples.english: We live on the eighth floor of the building.

examples.hanzi: 这是我第八次来这里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ dì bā cì lái zhèlǐ.
examples.english: This is my eighth time here.

meanings: variant of 老家伙[lao3 jia1 huo5]

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.

example.hanzi: 那个老家伙每天都在公园里下棋。
example.pinyin: nàge lǎojiāhuo měitiān dōu zài gōngyuán lǐ xiàqí.
example.english: That old fellow plays chess in the park every day.
example.fact: Chess is believed to have originated in northern India around the 6th century AD as a game called chaturanga, which spread through Persia and the Islamic world before reaching Europe by the 9th century, evolving along the way into the version played today.

examples.hanzi: 这个老家伙很会讲笑话。
examples.pinyin: Zhège lǎojiāhuo hěn huì jiǎng xiàohua.
examples.english: This old guy is good at telling jokes.

examples.hanzi: 别看他是个老家伙，跑得可快了。
examples.pinyin: Bié kàn tā shì ge lǎojiāhuo, pǎo de kě kuài le.
examples.english: Don't let his age fool you, that old fellow runs fast.

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
火 (fire) — flames; also in 灯 lamp, 烧 burn.
臽 (xiàn) is a loose clue; 陷 xiàn and 馅 xiàn share it.

example.hanzi: 蜡烛的火焰在风中轻轻摇晃。
example.pinyin: làzhú de huǒyàn zài fēng zhōng qīngqīng yáohuàng.
example.english: The candle's flame swayed gently in the wind.
example.fact: A candle flame appears blue at its base and yellow-orange at its tip because temperature varies sharply within it — the blue zone near the wick can exceed 1,400°C where combustion is most complete, while the visible yellow glow higher up comes from glowing, unburned soot particles.

examples.hanzi: 火焰把整个山谷都照亮了。
examples.pinyin: Huǒyàn bǎ zhěng ge shāngǔ dōu zhàoliàng le.
examples.english: The flames lit up the whole valley.

examples.hanzi: 炉子里的火焰越来越小。
examples.pinyin: Lúzi lǐ de huǒyàn yuè lái yuè xiǎo.
examples.english: The flame in the stove is getting smaller and smaller.

components.note: 音 (sound) — 言 (speech) with a stroke inside the mouth: a note within speech. 音 also gives 意 yì and 暗 àn.
乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 我们昨晚去听了一场古典音乐会。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zuówǎn qù tīng le yī chǎng gǔdiǎn yīnyuèhuì.
example.english: We went to a classical music concert last night.
example.fact: The Vienna Philharmonic's New Year's Concert, held every January 1st since 1939, is broadcast to more than 90 countries and an estimated audience of tens of millions, making it one of the most widely watched classical music events in the world.

examples.hanzi: 这个周末有一场免费的音乐会。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhōumò yǒu yì chǎng miǎnfèi de yīnyuèhuì.
examples.english: There is a free concert this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 我想和你一起去听音乐会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hé nǐ yìqǐ qù tīng yīnyuèhuì.
examples.english: I'd like to go to a concert with you.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 温 is warm, like lukewarm water.
昷 (wēn) gives the sound exactly: 温 wēn, also in 瘟 wēn.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 今天的温度比昨天低了很多。
example.pinyin: jīntiān de wēndù bǐ zuótiān dī le hěn duō.
example.english: Today's temperature is much lower than yesterday's.
example.fact: The lowest natural air temperature ever recorded on Earth's surface was -89.2°C, measured at Vostok Station in Antarctica in July 1983 — cold enough that exhaled breath can freeze into tiny ice crystals that make a faint hissing sound, an effect Siberians call "the whisper of stars."

examples.hanzi: 冰箱里的温度应该保持在四度左右。
examples.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ de wēndù yīnggāi bǎochí zài sì dù zuǒyòu.
examples.english: The temperature in the fridge should stay at around four degrees.

examples.hanzi: 你先量一下体温，看看温度正不正常。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān liáng yíxià tǐwēn, kànkan wēndù zhèng bu zhèngcháng.
examples.english: Take your body temperature first and see if it is normal.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — marks vessels and containers, as in 盒 box, 盘 plate, 盆 basin; 盐 is salt, once evaporated in dishes.

example.hanzi: 菜里的盐放多了。
example.pinyin: Cài lǐ de yán fàng duō le.
example.english: Too much salt was put in the dish.
example.fact: 盐 is salt, one of the "daily necessities" in the idiom 柴米油盐 (firewood, rice, oil, salt), meaning everyday household life. Related: 食盐 (table salt) and 海盐 (sea salt).

examples.hanzi: 请给我一点盐。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yìdiǎn yán.
examples.english: Please give me a little salt.

examples.hanzi: 这个汤太咸了，盐放多了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège tāng tài xián le, yán fàng duō le.
examples.english: The soup is too salty. Don't add any more salt.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌: 极 first meant a roof beam, the very top.
及 (jí) gives the exact sound; also in 级 jí and 吸 xī.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 长时间加班让他感到极度疲惫。
example.pinyin: cháng shíjiān jiābān ràng tā gǎndào jídù píbèi.
example.english: Working overtime for a long time left him feeling extremely exhausted.
example.fact: The longest documented period without sleep in a controlled study is about 11 days, endured by 17-year-old Randy Gardner in 1964 under scientific observation; researchers noted severe effects on his mood, concentration, and short-term memory well before that point, which is why such experiments are no longer conducted today.

examples.hanzi: 天气极度干燥，容易发生火灾。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì jídù gānzào, róngyì fāshēng huǒzāi.
examples.english: The weather is extremely dry, so fires break out easily.

examples.hanzi: 他极度需要一个安静的环境。
examples.pinyin: Tā jídù xūyào yí ge ānjìng de huánjìng.
examples.english: He badly needs a quiet environment.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.

example.hanzi: 请稍等,我马上帮您接通电话。
example.pinyin: qǐng shāo děng, wǒ mǎshàng bāng nín jiētōng diànhuà.
example.english: Please wait a moment, I'll connect your call right away.
example.fact: The first transatlantic telephone cable, TAT-1, was completed in 1956 between Scotland and Newfoundland, carrying just 36 simultaneous voice channels — a stark contrast to modern fiber-optic cables that can carry many terabits of data per second across the same ocean.

examples.hanzi: 电话打了很多次，终于接通了。
examples.pinyin: Diànhuà dǎ le hěn duō cì, zhōngyú jiētōng le.
examples.english: After many tries, the call finally went through.

examples.hanzi: 电源接通后，机器就开始工作。
examples.pinyin: Diànyuán jiētōng hòu, jīqì jiù kāishǐ gōngzuò.
examples.english: Once the power is connected, the machine starts working.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth family: 布, 带, 帽. Memory aid: a market stall with a cloth banner 巾 under a roof 亠, i.e. a 市 market.
柿 (shì, persimmon) — contains 市 as a sound part, same sound shì.
民 (people) — one old theory sees an eye pierced by a pointed tool, a mark of those with no rights; the meaning "ordinary people" is what to remember.

example.hanzi: 政府呼吁市民节约用水。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ hūhū shìmín jiéyuē yòngshuǐ.
example.english: The government is calling on city residents to conserve water.
example.fact: Cape Town, South Africa, came close to running out of municipal water entirely during a severe 2017-2018 drought, prompting the city to plan for a "Day Zero" when taps would be shut off; strict conservation by residents that cut usage nearly in half ultimately helped the city avoid the shutoff.

examples.hanzi: 这个公园是市民休闲的好地方。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gōngyuán shì shìmín xiūxián de hǎo dìfang.
examples.english: This park is a great place for city residents to relax.

examples.hanzi: 许多市民在广场上跳舞。
examples.pinyin: Xǔduō shìmín zài guǎngchǎng shàng tiàowǔ.
examples.english: Many townspeople dance in the square.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 深 is deep water.
罙 (shēn) — same sound — 深 is shēn; 罙 also sounds out 探 tàn.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 深 is deep water.
罙 (shēn) — same sound — 深 is shēn; 罙 also sounds out 探 tàn.

example.hanzi: 她深深地吸了一口气,然后开始演讲。
example.pinyin: tā shēnshēn de xī le yī kǒu qì, ránhòu kāishǐ yǎnjiǎng.
example.english: She took a deep breath and then began her speech.
example.fact: Freedivers competing without fins or breathing apparatus have descended past 100 meters on a single breath; the current world record for "no-limits" freediving exceeds 214 meters, a depth at which the human lungs compress to roughly a quarter of their surface volume under the pressure.

examples.hanzi: 他深深地爱着这片土地。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēnshēn de àizhe zhè piàn tǔdì.
examples.english: He loves this land deeply.

examples.hanzi: 这件事给我留下了深深的印象。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì gěi wǒ liúxià le shēnshēn de yìnxiàng.
examples.english: This left a deep impression on me.

components.note: 生 (to grow) — old forms of 青 show fresh growing plants plus pigment; the colour is fresh blue-green. 青 also sounds out 清, 请, 情, 晴.
小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 很多青少年喜欢在社交媒体上分享生活。
example.pinyin: hěn duō qīngshàonián xǐhuan zài shèjiāo méitǐ shàng fēnxiǎng shēnghuó.
example.english: Many teenagers like to share their lives on social media.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that the human prefrontal cortex, the brain region responsible for planning and impulse control, doesn't fully mature until around age 25 — a finding that has reshaped how researchers understand risk-taking behavior during adolescence.

examples.hanzi: 青少年需要充足的睡眠。
examples.pinyin: Qīngshàonián xūyào chōngzú de shuìmián.
examples.english: Teenagers need enough sleep.

examples.hanzi: 这本书是为青少年写的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū shì wèi qīngshàonián xiě de.
examples.english: This book was written for young people.

components.note: 王 (king) — the ruler below the crown-like top: 皇 is an emperor, as in 皇帝.
皇 (huáng) as a part sounds out 凰 huáng, 煌 huáng and 惶 huáng.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 皇家花园每年只对外开放几天。
example.pinyin: huángjiā huāyuán měinián zhǐ duìwài kāifàng jǐ tiān.
example.english: The royal garden is only open to the public a few days each year.
example.fact: The gardens of the Palace of Versailles took over 40 years and the labor of tens of thousands of workers to complete under Louis XIV, and the fountains were engineered with such complex hydraulics that a special canal was dug to divert water from the Seine just to keep them running.

examples.hanzi: 皇家卫队每天换岗一次。
examples.pinyin: Huángjiā wèiduì měi tiān huàngǎng yí cì.
examples.english: The royal guard changes shifts once a day.

examples.hanzi: 他们在皇家饭店举办了婚礼。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài Huángjiā Fàndiàn jǔbàn le hūnlǐ.
examples.english: They held their wedding at the Royal Hotel.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — wealth and payment, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
有 (to have) — owning wealth; 贿 is wealth given to buy favour.
贝 (shell, old money) — gifts of wealth, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
各 (gè) is a loose clue; 路 lù and 露 lù share it and sound exactly like 赂.

example.hanzi: 那名官员因受贿赂而被判入狱。
example.pinyin: nà míng guānyuán yīn shòu huìlù ér bèi pàn rùyù.
example.english: The official was sentenced to prison for accepting bribes.
example.fact: Transparency International has published its Corruption Perceptions Index every year since 1995, ranking over 180 countries by perceived levels of public-sector corruption — a tool now widely used by investors, aid agencies, and researchers to compare governance quality worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 他因为接受贿赂被开除了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi jiēshòu huìlù bèi kāichú le.
examples.english: He was fired for accepting a bribe.

examples.hanzi: 有人想用金钱来贿赂裁判。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén xiǎng yòng jīnqián lái huìlù cáipàn.
examples.english: Someone tried to bribe the referee with money.

components.note: 土 (earth) — earth radical — a base is something solid on the ground, as in 地, 城, 块.
其 (qí) — loose hint — 基 is jī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 这个项目基本上已经完成了。
example.pinyin: zhège xiàngmù jīběnshang yǐjīng wánchéng le.
example.english: This project is basically finished already.
example.fact: The Pareto principle, formulated by Italian economist Vilfredo Pareto in 1896 after he observed that roughly 80% of Italy's land was owned by 20% of the population, is now applied across fields from business to software engineering to describe how a small share of causes basically accounts for most outcomes.

examples.hanzi: 我基本上同意你的看法。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīběnshang tóngyì nǐ de kànfǎ.
examples.english: I basically agree with your view.

examples.hanzi: 基本上每个周末我都去爬山。
examples.pinyin: Jīběnshang měi ge zhōumò wǒ dōu qù páshān.
examples.english: Basically every weekend I go hiking.

components.note: 尸 (body/roof) — the top-left cover, as in 层 and 局. In 展 it works like a cover over cloth that is spread out; memory aid, shape is partly simplified.
衣 (clothing) — a bit of this sits inside 展. Dictionary story: laying out clothes to display them, hence 'unfold, exhibit' in 展示.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 消防队立即展开了搜救行动。
example.pinyin: xiāofáng duì lìjí zhǎnkāi le sōujiù xíngdòng.
example.english: The fire brigade immediately launched a search and rescue operation.
example.fact: The James Webb Space Telescope's sunshield, made of five ultra-thin layers of a material called Kapton, had to unfold in space using more than 100 release mechanisms after its 2021 launch — a process so complex that engineers called it one of the most technically risky deployments ever attempted.

examples.hanzi: 他把地图在桌子上展开了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ dìtú zài zhuōzi shàng zhǎnkāi le.
examples.english: He spread the map out on the table.

examples.hanzi: 两位老师就这个问题展开了讨论。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng wèi lǎoshī jiù zhège wèntí zhǎnkāi le tǎolùn.
examples.english: The two teachers launched a discussion on this issue.

components.note: 后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).
台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.

example.hanzi: 演出结束后,演员们都聚在后台聊天。
example.pinyin: yǎnchū jiéshù hòu, yǎnyuánmen dōu jù zài hòutái liáotiān.
example.english: After the show ended, the actors all gathered backstage to chat.
example.fact: The Sydney Opera House took 14 years to complete and its final cost of about $102 million was roughly 1,400% over the original 1957 budget estimate, largely because of the building's technically demanding stage machinery and sail-like roof structure.

examples.hanzi: 歌手在后台化妆，准备上台。
examples.pinyin: Gēshǒu zài hòutái huàzhuāng, zhǔnbèi shàngtái.
examples.english: The singer is putting on makeup backstage, getting ready to go on.

examples.hanzi: 听说他的后台很硬，没人敢得罪他。
examples.pinyin: Tīngshuō tā de hòutái hěn yìng, méi rén gǎn dézuì tā.
examples.english: They say he has strong backing, so nobody dares to offend him.

components.note: 上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.

example.hanzi: 周末我们常常去唱卡拉OK。
example.pinyin: zhōumò wǒmen chángcháng qù chàng kǎlā OK.
example.english: On weekends we often go sing karaoke.
example.fact: Karaoke was invented in Japan in 1971 by musician Daisuke Inoue, who built a machine called the "Juke 8" so bar patrons could sing along to instrumental tracks; he never patented the invention, later saying he regretted missing out on what became a multibillion-dollar global industry.

examples.hanzi: 我们去唱卡拉OK吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù chàng kǎlā OK ba.
examples.english: Let's go sing karaoke.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸最喜欢在卡拉OK里唱老歌。
examples.pinyin: Bàba zuì xǐhuan zài kǎlā OK lǐ chàng lǎo gē.
examples.english: Dad loves singing old songs at karaoke.

components.note: 宀 (roof, house) — a house family: 家 home, 安 safe, 室 room. 奥 originally meant the inner, dark corner of a house, hence 'mysterious, profound'.
米 (rice) — in the middle; the dictionary's story is a person finding a house full of rice. Memory aid, not proven.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: something big and hidden deep inside the house is mysterious.
斤 (axe) — the original idea was chopping with an axe, as in 新, 斩 chop, 断 break; today 斯 is mostly a sound-borrowing syllable sī in foreign names like 俄罗斯.
上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.

example.hanzi: 那部电影获得了今年的奥斯卡最佳影片奖。
example.pinyin: nà bù diànyǐng huòdé le jīnnián de àosīkǎ zuìjiā yǐngpiàn jiǎng.
example.english: That film won this year's Oscar for Best Picture.
example.fact: The Oscar statuette is officially named the "Academy Award of Merit" and stands 13.5 inches tall, plated in 24-karat gold over britannium metal; the nickname "Oscar" is popularly traced to a 1930s Academy librarian who joked the statue resembled her uncle Oscar.

examples.hanzi: 他梦想有一天能拿到奥斯卡奖。
examples.pinyin: Tā mèngxiǎng yǒu yì tiān néng ná dào Àosīkǎ jiǎng.
examples.english: He dreams of winning an Oscar one day.

examples.hanzi: 奥斯卡颁奖典礼将在周日举行。
examples.pinyin: Àosīkǎ bānjiǎng diǎnlǐ jiāng zài zhōurì jǔxíng.
examples.english: The Oscars ceremony will be held on Sunday.

components.note: 古 (gǔ) is a close sound clue for gù; 古 also in 姑 gū and 固 gù.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: an action with a cause.
阝 (hill, from 阜) on the left — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 陆, 附, 阶; 障 is a barrier.
章 (zhāng) hints at the sound: 障 zhàng is close, as in 彰 zhāng.

example.hanzi: 电梯发生故障,大家只能走楼梯。
example.pinyin: diàntī fāshēng gùzhàng, dàjiā zhǐ néng zǒu lóutī.
example.english: The elevator broke down, so everyone had to take the stairs.
example.fact: Modern passenger elevators are required to have multiple independent safety systems, a design tradition dating back to Elisha Otis's 1854 public demonstration in New York, where he had the cable of his elevator platform deliberately cut to show his safety brake would stop it from falling.

examples.hanzi: 我的电脑出了故障，开不了机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de diànnǎo chū le gùzhàng, kāi bù liǎo jī.
examples.english: My computer has a fault and won't start.

examples.hanzi: 工程师正在检查机器的故障。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī zhèngzài jiǎnchá jīqì de gùzhàng.
examples.english: The engineer is checking the machine's malfunction.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
口 (mouth) — marks speech and mouths, as in 叫, 问, 吃; selling is done with talk, as in 出售.

example.hanzi: 这套房子正在以低价出售。
example.pinyin: zhè tào fángzi zhèngzài yǐ dījià chūshòu.
example.english: This apartment is currently being sold at a low price.
example.fact: The most expensive private residence ever sold, Antilia in Mumbai, is estimated to be worth over $1 billion and includes 27 floors, three helipads, and a staff of roughly 600 people to maintain it for a single family.

examples.hanzi: 商店正在出售各种旧书。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn zhèngzài chūshòu gèzhǒng jiù shū.
examples.english: The shop is selling all kinds of used books.

examples.hanzi: 这家店不出售烟酒。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn bù chūshòu yānjiǔ.
examples.english: This shop does not sell cigarettes or alcohol.

components.note: 今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 那条河里曾经淘出过金子。
example.pinyin: nà tiáo hé lǐ céngjīng táo chū guò jīnzi.
example.english: Gold was once panned from that river.
example.fact: The California Gold Rush began in January 1848 when James Marshall found flakes of gold in the American River; within two years the news had drawn over 300,000 people to California from around the world, permanently reshaping the region's population and economy.

examples.hanzi: 这条项链是用真金子做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiàngliàn shì yòng zhēn jīnzi zuò de.
examples.english: This necklace is made of real gold.

examples.hanzi: 闪光的不一定都是金子。
examples.pinyin: Shǎnguāng de bù yídìng dōu shì jīnzi.
examples.english: All that glitters is not gold.

components.note: 亻 (person) — an older kinsman; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
白 (bái) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 泊 bó and 柏 bǎi.
爵 (wine cup) — 爵 was an ancient three-legged bronze wine cup, a mark of rank — so a noble title, as in 公爵.

example.hanzi: 那位伯爵拥有一座古老的城堡。
example.pinyin: nà wèi bójué yōngyǒu yī zuò gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
example.english: That earl owns an ancient castle.
example.fact: The title "earl" is the oldest of the English peerage ranks, dating back to Anglo-Saxon England before the Norman Conquest of 1066, when it referred to a regional governor known as an "eorl" — a rank later slotted between duke and viscount in the modern nobility system.

examples.hanzi: 那位伯爵很喜欢打猎。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi bójué hěn xǐhuan dǎliè.
examples.english: The earl loved hunting.

examples.hanzi: 伯爵夫人在花园里招待客人。
examples.pinyin: Bójué fūrén zài huāyuán lǐ zhāodài kèrén.
examples.english: The countess entertained guests in the garden.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
巫 — shaman: a ritual tool 工 with two figures 人 dancing on either side. 巫 wū also sounds out 诬 wū.

example.hanzi: 故事里的女巫住在森林深处的小屋里。
example.pinyin: gùshi lǐ de nǚwū zhù zài sēnlín shēnchù de xiǎo wū lǐ.
example.english: The witch in the story lives in a cottage deep in the forest.
example.fact: During the Salem witch trials of 1692-1693 in colonial Massachusetts, roughly 200 people were accused of witchcraft and 20 were executed; historians have since proposed explanations ranging from ergot fungus poisoning of rye grain to social tensions among rival families in the small Puritan settlement.

examples.hanzi: 童话里的女巫骑着扫帚飞行。
examples.pinyin: Tónghuà lǐ de nǚwū qízhe sàozhou fēixíng.
examples.english: The witch in the fairy tale flies on a broomstick.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们万圣节扮成了女巫。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen Wànshèngjié bàn chéng le nǚwū.
examples.english: The children dressed up as witches for Halloween.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ⺮ is bamboo, as in 笔, 筷, 箱; slips of bamboo were written on, so 签 is a slip or to sign.
佥 (qiān) — same sound — 签 is qiān; 佥 also sounds out 检 jiǎn and 脸 liǎn.
罒 (net, 四字头) — as in 罪 crime, 罗 net; 署 originally an office with a net of officials.
者 (zhě) gives a close sound; 暑 shǔ shares it and sounds exactly like 署.

example.hanzi: 两国领导人签署了和平协议。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó lǐngdǎorén qiānshǔle hépíng xiéyì.
example.english: The leaders of the two countries signed a peace agreement.
example.fact: The Peace of Westphalia, signed in 1648 to end the Thirty Years' War, was actually two treaties signed simultaneously in the German cities of Münster and Osnabrück, because Catholic and Protestant delegates refused to meet in the same room. Historians consider it a founding moment for the modern concept of state sovereignty.

examples.hanzi: 请在这里签署你的名字。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ qiānshǔ nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: Please sign your name here.

examples.hanzi: 公司和客户签署了一份长期合同。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī hé kèhù qiānshǔ le yí fèn chángqī hétong.
examples.english: The company and its client signed a long-term contract.

components.note: 饣 (food; traditional 食) — marks food and eating, as in 饭 meal, 饿 hungry, 饺 dumpling; 饱 is full from eating.
包 (bāo) — close sound: 饱 bǎo. 包 also sounds out 抱 bào and 跑 pǎo.

example.hanzi: 我吃饱了，谢谢。
example.pinyin: Wǒ chī bǎo le, xièxie.
example.english: I am full, thank you.
example.fact: 饱 usually attaches to 吃 as 吃饱, "eat until full." It is the polite way to refuse more food. Also 饱满 (plump), 饱和 (saturated), and 饱眼福 (to feast one's eyes). 吃饱了撑的 teases someone with too much time.

examples.hanzi: 早饭吃得太少，我现在还没饱。
examples.pinyin: Zǎofàn chī de tài shǎo, wǒ xiànzài hái méi bǎo.
examples.english: I ate too little for breakfast and I am still not full.

examples.hanzi: 你吃饱了没有？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ chībǎo le méiyǒu?
examples.english: Have you had enough to eat?

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical (犬), as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 猜 once meant a suspicious, wary animal.
青 (qīng) — near sound — 猜 is cāi; 青 also sounds out 清, 请, 情 and 晴.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water: 河, 深, 浅; 测 was measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) is close to cè; same part in 侧 cè and 厕 cè.

example.hanzi: 科学家们对恐龙灭绝的原因提出了许多猜测。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen duì kǒnglóng mièjué de yuányīn tíchūle xǔduō cāicè.
example.english: Scientists have proposed many conjectures about the cause of dinosaur extinction.
example.fact: The leading explanation for the dinosaur extinction 66 million years ago is a 10-kilometer-wide asteroid that struck what is now the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico, leaving the Chicxulub crater. Geologist Walter Alvarez and his father proposed the theory in 1980 after finding a worldwide layer of iridium-rich clay dating to exactly that time.

examples.hanzi: 我猜测他今天不会来了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cāicè tā jīntiān bú huì lái le.
examples.english: I guess he won't be coming today.

examples.hanzi: 这只是我的猜测，没有证据。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì wǒ de cāicè, méiyǒu zhèngjù.
examples.english: This is just my guess, with no evidence.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.

example.hanzi: 相比其他行星，金星的表面温度极高。
example.pinyin: Xiāngbǐ qítā xíngxīng, Jīnxīng de biǎomiàn wēndù jí gāo.
example.english: Compared to other planets, Venus's surface temperature is extremely high.
example.fact: Venus's surface reaches about 465°C, hot enough to melt lead, even though Mercury sits closer to the sun. The cause is a runaway greenhouse effect: a thick atmosphere of carbon dioxide traps heat so effectively that Venus stays hotter than any other planet in the solar system.

examples.hanzi: 相比去年，今年的雨水多了很多。
examples.pinyin: Xiāngbǐ qùnián, jīnnián de yǔshuǐ duō le hěn duō.
examples.english: Compared with last year, there's been much more rain this year.

examples.hanzi: 两家店相比，我更喜欢这一家。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng jiā diàn xiāngbǐ, wǒ gèng xǐhuan zhè yì jiā.
examples.english: Comparing the two shops, I prefer this one.

components.note: 又 (hand) — 双 (simplified 雙) shows two birds held in one hand: a pair; the simplified form just doubles the hand 又又.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 双方经过长时间谈判终于达成了协议。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng jīngguò cháng shíjiān tánpàn zhōngyú dáchéngle xiéyì.
example.english: Both sides finally reached an agreement after lengthy negotiations.
example.fact: The 1978 Camp David Accords between Egypt and Israel were hammered out over 13 tense days at the US presidential retreat in Maryland, mediated personally by President Jimmy Carter. The resulting treaty made Egypt the first Arab nation to formally recognize Israel.

examples.hanzi: 双方都同意推迟会议。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng dōu tóngyì tuīchí huìyì.
examples.english: Both sides agreed to postpone the meeting.

examples.hanzi: 这对双方都有好处。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duì shuāngfāng dōu yǒu hǎochù.
examples.english: This benefits both parties.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.

example.hanzi: 科学家精确测量了这批样本的数量。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā jīngquè cèliángle zhè pī yàngběn de shùliàng.
example.english: Scientists precisely measured the quantity of this batch of samples.
example.fact: Avogadro's number, roughly 6.022×10²³, defines the quantity of particles in one mole of any substance — a number so large that one mole of standard sheets of paper stacked up would reach far beyond the width of the observable universe. It's named after Amedeo Avogadro, who never actually calculated the number himself; it was named in his honor decades after his death.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的顾客数量越来越多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de gùkè shùliàng yuè lái yuè duō.
examples.english: The number of customers at this shop keeps growing.

examples.hanzi: 质量比数量更重要。
examples.pinyin: Zhìliàng bǐ shùliàng gèng zhòngyào.
examples.english: Quality matters more than quantity.

components.note: 罒 (net) — 罒 is a net, as in 罚, 置; 罗 is a net, and is mostly seen in 罗马 Rome.
亻 (person) — an older kinsman; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
白 (bái) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 泊 bó and 柏 bǎi.
牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 罗伯特在会议上介绍了新的研究成果。
example.pinyin: Luóbótè zài huìyì shàng jièshàole xīn de yánjiū chéngguǒ.
example.english: Robert presented new research findings at the meeting.
example.fact: English scientist Robert Hooke coined the biological term 'cell' in 1665 after examining a thin slice of cork under a microscope he built himself and noticing tiny box-like compartments that reminded him of monks' rooms, or cells, in a monastery. His book Micrographia was one of the first to popularize the microscopic world.

examples.hanzi: 罗伯特是我的邻居，他很爱养花。
examples.pinyin: Luóbótè shì wǒ de línjū, tā hěn ài yǎng huā.
examples.english: Robert is my neighbor, and he loves growing flowers.

examples.hanzi: 你认识罗伯特吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Luóbótè ma?
examples.english: Do you know Robert?

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.

example.hanzi: 对了，你知道长颈鹿的心脏比人的心脏大得多吗？
example.pinyin: Duì le, nǐ zhīdào chángjǐnglù de xīnzàng bǐ rén de xīnzàng dà de duō ma?
example.english: Oh, by the way, did you know a giraffe's heart is much bigger than a human heart?
example.fact: A giraffe's heart can weigh up to 11 kilograms and generates roughly double the blood pressure of most other mammals, which it needs to pump blood all the way up its long neck to the brain, about six meters above the ground. Special valves and tight skin in the legs also prevent blood from pooling when the giraffe lowers its head to drink.

examples.hanzi: 对了，明天几点开会？
examples.pinyin: Duì le, míngtiān jǐ diǎn kāihuì?
examples.english: Oh, by the way, what time is the meeting tomorrow?

examples.hanzi: 你的答案对了，真聪明。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de dá'àn duì le, zhēn cōngmíng.
examples.english: Your answer is correct, how smart.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — marks boats, as in 船 ship, 航 sail; 舱 is a ship's cabin.
仓 (cāng) — same sound: 舱 cāng. 仓 also sounds out 苍 cāng and 沧 cāng.

example.hanzi: 飞机的经济舱座位比较小。
example.pinyin: Fēijī de jīngjìcāng zuòwèi bǐjiào xiǎo.
example.english: The seats in a plane's economy class are rather small.
example.fact: 舱 started out as a ship's compartment, and now covers aircraft and spacecraft: 机舱 (cabin), 经济舱 (economy class), 商务舱 (business class), 头等舱 (first class), 太空舱 (space capsule).

examples.hanzi: 乘客们请回到自己的座舱。
examples.pinyin: Chéngkèmen qǐng huídào zìjǐ de zuòcāng.
examples.english: Passengers, please return to your own seats.

examples.hanzi: 船舱里很闷，我想去外面。
examples.pinyin: Chuáncāng lǐ hěn mēn, wǒ xiǎng qù wàimiàn.
examples.english: It is stuffy in the cabin, and I want to go outside.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — marks the head, as in 顺, 领, 额 forehead; 颈 is the neck.

example.hanzi: 他的颈部有点痛。
example.pinyin: Tā de jǐngbù yǒudiǎn tòng.
example.english: His neck hurts a bit.
example.fact: 颈 is the formal or medical word for neck; everyday speech uses 脖子. 颈椎 (cervical vertebrae) is a famous complaint of office workers, and the giraffe is 长颈鹿, "long-neck deer." In 脖颈 it takes the reading gěng.

examples.hanzi: 长颈鹿的脖子很长。
examples.pinyin: Chángjǐnglù de bózi hěn cháng.
examples.english: A giraffe has a very long neck.

examples.hanzi: 他坐了很久，颈椎有点不舒服。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò le hěn jiǔ, jǐngzhuī yǒudiǎn bù shūfu.
examples.english: He sat for a long time, and his neck feels a bit uncomfortable.

components.note: 匸 (a hiding box, open at the side) — the frame around 儿. Rare radical, not meaningful on its own.
儿 (legs) — the legs below. Memory aid: 匹 counts horses (一匹马) — think of a horse's legs under a covering, or a bolt of cloth rolled up.
酉 (wine jar) — marks wine and brewing, as in 酒, 醉 drunk, 醒; 配 first meant mixing wine, then matching.
己 (jǐ) is only a loose sound hint for pèi.

example.hanzi: 这个算法能快速匹配指纹数据库中的记录。
example.pinyin: Zhège suànfǎ néng kuàisù pǐpèi zhǐwén shùjùkù zhōng de jìlù.
example.english: This algorithm can quickly match records in the fingerprint database.
example.fact: Human fingerprints are fully formed by about the seventeenth week of fetal development and stay the same for life outside of scarring, which is why they remain a reliable form of identification. The FBI's fingerprint database, now called the Next Generation Identification system, holds records for well over 100 million people.

examples.hanzi: 软件会自动匹配最合适的座位。
examples.pinyin: Ruǎnjiàn huì zìdòng pǐpèi zuì héshì de zuòwèi.
examples.english: The software automatically matches the most suitable seat.

examples.hanzi: 这双鞋和你的衣服很匹配。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié hé nǐ de yīfu hěn pǐpèi.
examples.english: These shoes match your outfit well.

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — blocked openings; also in 空 empty, 窗 window, 突 sudden.
至 (zhì) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 致 zhì and 室 shì.
自 (nose) — over 心 heart: breath comes through the nose from the heart, so rest, news.

example.hanzi: 潜水员必须小心避免因缺氧而窒息。
example.pinyin: Qiánshuǐyuán bìxū xiǎoxīn bìmiǎn yīn quēyǎng ér zhìxī.
example.english: Divers must be careful to avoid suffocating from lack of oxygen.
example.fact: The human brain can typically survive only about four to six minutes without oxygen before permanent damage begins. Elite free divers train their bodies to trigger the mammalian dive reflex, which slows the heart rate and redirects blood to vital organs, allowing some to hold their breath for over ten minutes underwater.

examples.hanzi: 他吃得太快，差点窒息。
examples.pinyin: Tā chī de tài kuài, chàdiǎn zhìxī.
examples.english: He ate so fast that he nearly choked.

examples.hanzi: 房间里空气不流通，让人觉得窒息。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ kōngqì bù liútōng, ràng rén juéde zhìxī.
examples.english: The air in the room doesn't circulate, making people feel stifled.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a stiff body; also in 你 you, 体 body.
畺 (jiāng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 疆 jiāng and 缰 jiāng.
尸 (body) — originally a person seated or lying; as a radical it is in 尾 tail, 层 floor, 居 reside, 屋 house.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了僵尸入侵城市的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle jiāngshī rùqīn chéngshì de gùshì.
example.english: This movie tells the story of zombies invading a city.
example.fact: In tropical forests, a real fungus called Ophiocordyceps unilateralis infects carpenter ants and hijacks their nervous system, forcing the ant to climb vegetation and clamp its jaws onto a leaf in a spot ideal for the fungus, before a spore-releasing stalk erupts from the dead ant's head. Scientists sometimes call it the 'zombie ant fungus.'

examples.hanzi: 万圣节时，孩子们喜欢扮成僵尸。
examples.pinyin: Wànshèngjié shí, háizimen xǐhuan bàn chéng jiāngshī.
examples.english: At Halloween, kids like to dress up as zombies.

examples.hanzi: 这款游戏里有很多僵尸。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuǎn yóuxì lǐ yǒu hěn duō jiāngshī.
examples.english: There are lots of zombies in this game.

components.note: 象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.
彳 (step, 双人旁) — walking and journeys, as in 行 go, 往 toward, 得; 征 is a march or campaign.
正 (zhèng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 证 zhèng, 政 zhèng and 整 zhěng.

example.hanzi: 白鸽常常被视为和平的象征。
example.pinyin: Báigē chángcháng bèi shìwéi hépíng de xiàngzhēng.
example.english: The white dove is often regarded as a symbol of peace.
example.fact: Doves and pigeons are among the very few birds, along with penguins and flamingos, that feed their chicks a nutrient-rich fluid called 'crop milk,' regurgitated from a pouch in their throat rather than food caught in the wild. Both parents produce and share this feeding duty equally.

examples.hanzi: 红色是好运的象征。
examples.pinyin: Hóngsè shì hǎoyùn de xiàngzhēng.
examples.english: Red is a symbol of good luck.

examples.hanzi: 这座塔象征着这座城市的历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò tǎ xiàngzhēng zhe zhè zuò chéngshì de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This tower symbolizes the history of the city.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
亻 (person) — one who relies on arms; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
丈 (zhàng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 杖 zhàng.

example.hanzi: 古代士兵常常骑马打仗。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài shìbīng chángcháng qímǎ dǎzhàng.
example.english: Ancient soldiers often fought battles on horseback.
example.fact: The stirrup, likely invented in China or Central Asia around the 4th century AD, let mounted soldiers grip their horse securely with their legs and fight with both hands free. Historians credit this simple device with transforming cavalry warfare and helping give rise to the heavily armored knights of medieval Europe.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在院子里玩打仗的游戏。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài yuànzi lǐ wán dǎzhàng de yóuxì.
examples.english: The kids are playing a war game in the yard.

examples.hanzi: 他爷爷年轻时曾经去前线打仗。
examples.pinyin: Tā yéye niánqīng shí céngjīng qù qiánxiàn dǎzhàng.
examples.english: His grandfather went to the front to fight when he was young.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) on the right, as in 到, 别, 利; 创 first meant a cut wound and then to create.
仓 (cāng) — near sound — 创 is chuàng; 仓 also sounds out 抢 qiǎng and 枪 qiāng.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 贝多芬在失聪后仍坚持创作音乐。
example.pinyin: Bèiduōfēn zài shīcōng hòu réng jiānchí chuàngzuò yīnyuè.
example.english: Beethoven continued composing music even after losing his hearing.
example.fact: Beethoven began losing his hearing in his late twenties and was almost completely deaf by the time he composed his Ninth Symphony. He reportedly sawed the legs off a piano and set it on the floor so he could feel the vibrations of the notes through the wood and his own body.

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢在安静的早晨创作。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài ānjìng de zǎochén chuàngzuò.
examples.english: She likes to create in the quiet mornings.

examples.hanzi: 这幅画是他晚年的创作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà shì tā wǎnnián de chuàngzuò.
examples.english: This painting is a work from his later years.

components.note: 片 (slice, plank) — marks flat pieces and wooden boards; 牌 is a signboard, a card or a tile.
卑 (bēi) hints at the sound: 牌 pái is close to 脾 pí, which shares it.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 商店门口挂着一个写着营业中的牌子。
example.pinyin: Shāngdiàn ménkǒu guàzhe yí gè xiězhe yíngyè zhōng de páizi.
example.english: A sign reading 'Open' hangs at the shop's entrance.
example.fact: The Bass Brewery's red triangle logo became the United Kingdom's first officially registered trademark in 1876, the day the new Trade Marks Registration Act took effect, after an employee reportedly camped outside the registry office overnight to be first in line.

examples.hanzi: 这个牌子的运动鞋很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhège páizi de yùndòngxié hěn shūfu.
examples.english: This brand of sneakers is very comfortable.

examples.hanzi: 路边的牌子上写着“禁止停车”。
examples.pinyin: Lùbiān de páizi shàng xiězhe “jìnzhǐ tíngchē”.
examples.english: The sign by the road reads “No Parking”.
